checks.name: Real native setModel round trip preserves exact JSONL messages, header and creation fingerprint

Crash after intent: reopen real native file and SQLite, recover once, no replay on second recovery
Crash after native: reopen real native file and SQLite, recover once, no replay on second recovery
Crash after receipt: reopen real native file and SQLite, recover once, no replay on second recovery
Crash after committed: reopen real native file and SQLite, recover once, no replay on second recovery
Aborted pre-native intent allows a later native switch without resurrecting old request
Concurrent durable prepare and stale CAS rejected across independent SQLite handles
Binding conflict rolls back transition and ledger in the same SQLite statement
Archiving between native receipt and commit atomically rejects, never unarchives or aborts actual native change
Runtime host lock, permission denial and Hana target context guard reject before native intent
Hana uses current context usage and token-estimation fallback with its original capacity reserve
Unrecorded native model_change cannot be accepted because it matches a target model string
Native mutation throwing after appendModelChange is recoverable without calling setModel again
Foreign native identity/file and unsafe saved path rejected without mutating history
Altered native receipt rejected with ledger unchanged
Unexpected user/tool/compaction history inside a pending idle switch cannot be adopted
Ledger revision conflict rolls back binding and transition, recovery requires exact original revision
Authority isolation branch cannot silently restore removed model markers or old messages in B1
Unknown ledger schema and malformed native IDs fail closed
Already-selected model is a real no-op with no new native entries or revision bump
Damaged native JSONL cannot be silently tolerated by SDK during identity mutation
A stale cached manager cannot overwrite or adopt another file writer
Duplicate IDs and cyclic parents rejected before native branch traversal
All actual native switching and recovery instances make zero provider requests
Neither transition persistence nor native history contains the synthetic credential
